target_customer: Consumers and clinicians who want early cancer screening at home; payer and channel not stated in sources opened
problem: Cancer screening is slow and needs lab visits. The company is building rapid at-home urine tests with results in about 30 minutes, starting with prostate, bladder and ovarian cancers.
business_model: Diagnostics product, commercial model not stated in sources opened
product_category: At-home cancer screening diagnostics (synthetic biology, machine learning, computer vision)

founders.name: Luca Springer
education: University of Oxford, MSc Computer Science and MSc Global Governance, Rhodes Scholar
founders.background_notes: YC page says network science, computational game theory and healthcare policy focus; Schmidt Futures ISF Fellow.

founders.name: Thomas Carroll
education: Rhodes Scholar (per YC launch post, institution not stated on page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says clinical cancer researcher specializing in bioinformatics, biomarkers and methods development.

technical_complexity.rationale: A reliable 30 minute at-home multi-cancer urine test combines synthetic biology assays with computer vision and machine learning, and would need clinical validation and regulatory clearance.

defensibility.rationale: If validated, clinical data and regulatory clearance would be hard to copy, but no clearance or validation is documented in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows incumbents copying the at-home rapid urine approach.

market_need_then: Screening gaps exist for cancers such as prostate, bladder and ovarian, and the company pitches the test as easy as a pregnancy test. No third-party demand data was opened.

branding.domain_note: Moved from a cleancard domain to numen.com after the rename; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: mission driven; tagline 'A lab in every hand'

rebrands.why: Not stated; legal entity remains Cleancard Inc. per aggregator profiles. Year is from a secondary timeline.

brand_strength.rationale: A rename from Cleancard to a shorter name and a tagline, but no press or community evidence about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Numen, formerly Cleancard, is active with 18 people per the YC page and is developing rapid at-home cancer tests. Technical risk and regulatory path are the main unknowns, and no verified funding, clearance or shutdown information was found. The outcome search surfaced no coverage of the company.
notes: Aggregator snippets report a roughly $5M seed in September 2023 and a PitchBook Series A in October 2024, all unverified and mutually inconsistent, so no rounds are recorded. Competitors Galleri and Exact Sciences come only from an undated commercial profile, so the competitor list is empty. The rename year (2024) comes from secondary sources. YC page launched as Cleancard.
